text:
devin: Kicking off perf validation for the new ca-central-1 GPU pool (A100-80GB). Running the smoke/bench suite now — tagging @sasha @maria for driver/kernel checks and @aj for handoff.
sasha: thanks. quick checklist before benchmarks: kernel >= 5.15, nvidia-driver 525+, CUDA 12.0 or 12.1, nvidia-container-runtime installed. also confirm NVLink topology (we need full NVLink for multi-GPU baselining).
maria: confirmed kernel 5.15.0-101 and driver 525.105.17 on all nodes. CUDA 12.1 runtime present. nvlink looks good on the first 4 nodes, nodes 5/6 reporting missing link between GPU1-GPU2.
devin: noted re: nodes 5/6. Running quick PCI/NV checks:
```
ssh node-05 'nvidia-smi topo --matrix'
ssh node-05 'lspci | grep -i nvidia'
```
aj: I'll queue a hardware ticket for node-05 and node-06, but proceed with single-GPU baselines for now.
infra-bot: cluster-ca-central-1: nodes 01-08 provisioned, kube nodes ready, storage PVs bound. :white_check_mark:
sasha: perf commands I want run (short):
- run rw-infer bench (single stream) for seq_len=1024, batch=1
- run rw-infer bench (batched) for batch=8 and batch=32
- kernel driver memtest: run `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` and `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced` for OOM/driver hangs
devin: starting single-GPU baseline (seq=1024, batch=1). script: `tools/bench/run_infer.py --model mosaicml/mpt-7b --sequence 1024 --batch 1 --iters 100` will give tokens/sec and p99.
maria: quick note: set `ulimit -l` to unlimited and `vm.nr_hugepages` tuned to 2048 on nodes, otherwise memory allocation fails during large sequence runs.
aj: run started, ETA ~10m.
(devin pasted results):
```
node-01 single-GPU seq=1024 batch=1: 430 tokens/s, p50=45ms, p95=110ms, p99=220ms
node-02 single-GPU seq=1024 batch=1: 425 tokens/s, p50=46ms, p95=115ms, p99=230ms
```
sasha: those single-GPU numbers look fine. Target was >=400 tokens/s and p99 <300ms for single-stream. Pass.
devin: moving to batched runs (batch=8 then 32) to measure throughput/cost tradeoffs.
(devin pasted batched results):
```
node-01 batch=8: 3100 tokens/s (amortized), avg latency per request=320ms
node-01 batch=32: 9000 tokens/s, avg latency per request=980ms
```
maria: batch=8 looks good for latency-sensitive endpoints. batch=32 is only for high-throughput offline jobs.
sasha: driver/kernel check results: `dmesg` shows one warning on node-06 (GPU reset logged), need to follow up before enabling it as production.
aj: flagged node-06 in inventory, will put in maintenance and swap PCI riser with on-call vendor tech tomorrow. For throughput planning, we should assume only nodes 01-04 and 07-08 are green.
devin: network baseline: measured egress to model registry and S3 (100GB blobs). Using curl and iperf:
```
iperf3 -c storage-ca-central-1: avg 9.2 Gbps
curl -sS -w '%{time_total}' -o /dev/null https://models.internal/model.tar  # ~0.8s
```
sasha: 9.2Gbps looks low for multi-GPU pulls at scale. Are these nodes on 25Gbps NICs? check `ethtool` and CNI config.
maria: NIC is 25Gbps but jumbo frames disabled. Enabling jumbo frames (+MTU 9000) bump iperf to ~23Gbps in my quick test on node-02.
devin: re-ran model pull with MTU 9000: download reduced to 0.3s — good for startup latencies when pulling weights.
sasha: final pass/fail criteria we agreed on:
- single-GPU seq=1024 batch=1 tokens/s >= 400, p99 < 300ms
- batch=8 throughput >= 3k tokens/s and per-request avg latency <350ms
- no kernel driver resets in logs during 30m soak
- NVLink connectivity correct for GPU pairing or node fenced out
- network MTU >= 9000 or observed >20Gbps
devin: current status: nodes 01-04,07-08 meet criteria. node-05 minor NVLink mismatch (ticket open), node-06 has driver reset (maintenance). Marking cluster as PARTIAL-PROD (can accept dedicated jobs but not critical low-latency traffic).
aj: noted. I'll update capacity docs and set autoscaler headroom to avoid scheduling low-latency pods on nodes 05/06. Also will open an internal PR to document the `mtu=9000` requirement in the region bootstrap runbook.
maria: handoff steps for SRE/ops:
1) add nodes 01-04,07-08 to production pool tag `ca-central-1:prod-ready`
2) add node-05, node-06 to `maintenance` with owner `aj`
3) update console dashboard to show p99 and tokens/s per node
4) schedule 4h soak test (run bench suite every 30s) and alert on driver OOM/resets
devin: I'll post the final perf summary and attach the bench logs to the ticket. anything else?
sasha: one more: add a kernel boot arg `intel_iommu=on` for nodes with NVLink RDMA paths per vendor note; will test on node-07 tomorrow.
infra-bot: ticket #INF-2241 created for node-06 driver-reset. ticket #INF-2242 created for node-05 NVLink riser. :ticket:
aj: thanks all — follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30PT to confirm hardware fixes and promote nodes to full prod.
devin: thanks folks :rocket:
